blockers.corrected_root_cause: AETHER_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH in the production .env is itself a bcrypt hash of the literal string "admin123" - the operator/owner admin password IS admin123. orchestrator_corrections.reality: FALSE - the dashboard is CORRECT and internally consistent. get_application_counts() (app/routers/analytics.py:31, the RT-004 contract) deliberately counts DISTINCT JOBS, not raw Application rows, to avoid inflating counts with cover-letter re-draft/version rows - live evidence found ONE job with 9 letter-version rows. Independent SQL run this session: COUNT(DISTINCT jobId) WHERE status<>'draft' = 47, and of those 45 within 7 days - matching the UI's "47" and "+45 this week" EXACTLY. UI = API = live DB.
orchestrator_corrections.lesson: My "74" baseline was a RAW-ROW count - a different, non-comparable metric from what the product intentionally displays. I propagated it into multiple screen briefs as if it were ground truth. Baselines must record the PREDICATE, not just the number.
orchestrator_corrections.consequence: This also explains WHY RT-004 exists and why its strict-equality guard is load-bearing - it protects exactly this jobs-not-rows contract. Reinforces that the concurrent RT-004 adjudication must preserve the protection, with the tamper-proof, rather than simply relaxing the assertion.
